text: S7 classes formal definition create new_class(). two arguments ’ll use almost every class: name class, supplied first argument. class properties, data associated instance class. easiest way define properties supply named list values define valid types property. following code defines simple dog class two properties: character name numeric age. {r} Dog <- new_class("Dog", properties = list(   name = class_character,   age = class_numeric )) Dog S7 provides number built-definitions allow refer existing base types S7 classes. can recognize definitions start class_. Note ’ve assigned return value new_class() object name class. important! object represents class use construct instances class: {r} lola <- Dog(name = "Lola", age = 11) lola S7 object, can get set properties using @: {r} lola@age <- 12 lola@age S7 automatically validates type property using type supplied new_class(): {r, error = TRUE} lola@age <- "twelve" Given object, can retrieve class S7_class(): {r} S7_class(lola) S7 objects also S3 class(). used compatibility existing S3 generics can learn vignette("compatibility"). {r} class(lola) want learn details S7 classes objects, including validation methods details properties, please see vignette("classes-objects").

text: S7, like S3 S4, built around idea generic functions, generics short. generic defines interface, uses different implementation depending class one arguments. implementation specific class called method, generic finds appropriate method performing method dispatch. Use new_generic() create S7 generic. simplest form, needs two arguments: name generic (used error messages) name argument used method dispatch: {r} speak <- new_generic("speak", "x") Like new_class(), always assign result new_generic() variable name first argument. generic, can register methods specific classes method(generic, class) <- implementation. {r} method(speak, Dog) <- function(x) {   "Woof" } method registered, generic use appropriate: {r} speak(lola) Let’s define another class, one cats, define another method speak(): ```{r} Cat <- new_class(“Cat”, properties = list( name = class_character, age = class_double )) method(speak, Cat) <- function(x) { “Meow” } fluffy <- Cat(name = “Fluffy”, age = 5) speak(fluffy)
code: You get an error if you call the generic with a class that doesn't have a method:  ```{r, error = TRUE} speak(1)

text: cat dog classes share properties, use common parent class extract duplicated specification. first define parent class: {r} Pet <- new_class("Pet",   properties = list(     name = class_character,     age = class_numeric   ) ) use parent argument new_class: ```{r} Cat <- new_class(“Cat”, parent = Pet) Dog <- new_class(“Dog”, parent = Pet) Cat Dog Method dispatch takes advantage hierarchy parent classes: method defined class, try method parent class, finds method gives error. inheritance powerful mechanism sharing code across classes. ```{r} describe <- new_generic(“describe”, “x”) method(describe, Pet) <- function(x) { paste0(x@name, ” “, x@age,” years old”) } describe(lola) describe(fluffy) method(describe, Dog) <- function(x) { paste0(x@name, ” “, x@age,” year old dog”) } describe(lola) describe(fluffy) Printing generic show methods currently defined: {r} describe can use method() retrieve implementation one methods: {r} method(describe, Pet)
code: Because we have created new classes, we need to recreate the existing `lola` and `fluffy` objects:  ```{r} lola <- Dog(name = "Lola", age = 11) fluffy <- Cat(name = "Fluffy", age = 5) You can define a fallback method for any S7 object by registering a method for `S7_object`:  ```{r} method(describe, S7_object) <- function(x) {   "An S7 object" }  Cocktail <- new_class("Cocktail",   properties = list(     ingredients = class_character   ) ) martini <- Cocktail(ingredients = c("gin", "vermouth")) describe(martini)

code: library(shiny) library(shinyOAuth)  client <- oauth_client(   provider = oauth_provider_spotify(),   client_id = Sys.getenv("SPOTIFY_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID"),   client_secret = Sys.getenv("SPOTIFY_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET"),   redirect_uri = "http://127.0.0.1:8100",   scopes = c("user-read-private", "user-top-read"),   resource_bases = c(spotify = "https://api.spotify.com/v1") )  ui <- oauth_ui(fluidPage(   h2("My top tracks"),   actionButton("load", "Load top tracks"),   tableOutput("tracks") ), id = "auth", client = client)  server <- function(input, output, session) {   auth <- oauth_module_server("auth", client)   tracks <- reactiveVal(NULL)    observe({     connection <- auth[["connection"]]()     result <- isolate(tracks())     if (is.null(connection) ||         !connection[["has_scopes"]]("user-top-read") ||         (!is.null(result) &&          !identical(result[["authorization"]], connection[["id"]]))) {       tracks(NULL)     }   })    observeEvent(input[["load"]], {     connection <- req(auth[["connection"]]())     req(connection[["has_scopes"]]("user-top-read"))     data <- tryCatch({       response <- connection[["request"]](         "spotify", "me/top/tracks",         query = list(limit = 10, time_range = "short_term"),         required_scopes = "user-top-read",         refresh = TRUE       )       httr2::resp_check_status(response)       body <- httr2::resp_body_json(response, simplifyVector = FALSE)       vapply(body[["items"]], function(track) track[["name"]], character(1))     }, error = function(e) NULL)     tracks(list(authorization = connection[["id"]], data = data))   })    output[["tracks"]] <- renderTable({     connection <- req(auth[["connection"]]())     req(connection[["has_scopes"]]("user-top-read"))     result <- tracks()     req(identical(result[["authorization"]], connection[["id"]]))     values <- result[["data"]]     validate(need(!is.null(values), "Could not load tracks. Try again later."))     validate(need(length(values) > 0, "No listening data to show yet."))     data.frame(Track = values)   }) }  runApp(shinyApp(ui, server), port = 8100, launch.browser = FALSE)

title: Package options reference
text: options control diagnostic events request details contain. options(shinyOAuth.audit_hook = function(event){ ... }) – receive structured audit error events options(shinyOAuth.audit_include_http = FALSE) – exclude HTTP request details audit events (default: TRUE) options(shinyOAuth.audit_include_raw_session_token = TRUE) – include raw shiny_session[["token"]] native audit-hook payloads. default, hooks receive shiny_session[["session_token_digest"]] options(shinyOAuth.audit_redact_http = FALSE) – disable automatic redaction sensitive data audit events (default: TRUE). Debug : raw mode can expose cookies, authorization headers, codes, state values, client IP addresses options(shinyOAuth.telemetry_path_scrubber = function(path) NULL) – return approved route labels audit OTel paths, omitted default. Return NULL unknown routes, remove identifying segments, make function idempotent. options(shinyOAuth.audit_digest_key = ...) – shared HMAC-SHA256 key least 32 bytes audit/OTel correlation. default random per-process key; invalid configured keys cause error. options(shinyOAuth.otel_tracing_enabled = FALSE) – disable ‘shinyOAuth’ OpenTelemetry span creation async trace-context propagation. Default: TRUE options(shinyOAuth.otel_logging_enabled = FALSE) – disable ‘shinyOAuth’ OpenTelemetry log emission. Default: TRUE options(shinyOAuth.otel_include_authorization_details = TRUE) – include raw scope names, claim targets, ACR values telemetry. Default: FALSE (counts ). fields can reveal private information produce many distinct telemetry values. See Audit logging R hook examples OpenTelemetry log trace exporter setup.

title: Package options reference
text: Network settings limit request duration response size. options(shinyOAuth.tls_min_version = "1.2") - require TLS 1.2 later package HTTPS requests (default). Use "1.3" higher minimum; absent option NULL restores TLS 1.2. Set discovery login. applies async workers ; browser reverse-proxy TLS must configured separately. options(shinyOAuth.timeout = 5) – default HTTP timeout (seconds) applied outbound requests (discovery, JWKS, token exchange, userinfo). Increase provider/network slow. Values beyond curl’s supported timeout range capped options(shinyOAuth.retry_max_tries = 3L) – maximum attempts network errors HTTP 408, 429 5xx responses. Code exchange refresh skip automatic retries, apart one DPoP nonce-challenge retry. options(shinyOAuth.dpop_nonce_max_bytes = 4096L) – maximum DPoP nonce size bytes; supported range 1 65536. options(shinyOAuth.retry_backoff_base = 0.5) – base backoff seconds used exponential backoff jitter options(shinyOAuth.retry_backoff_cap = 5) – per‑attempt cap backoff seconds (jitter) options(shinyOAuth.retry_after_cap = 60) – maximum synchronous sleep seconds server-provided Retry-value; separate client-side backoff cap options(shinyOAuth.retry_status = c(408L, 429L, 500:599)) – HTTP statuses considered transient retried options(shinyOAuth.user_agent = "shinyOAuth/<version> R/<version> httr2/<version>") – override HTTP User-Agent. default includes installed package R versions. options(shinyOAuth.allow_redirect = FALSE) – reject redirects sensitive provider requests default. opt-permits redirects sessions, potentially forwarding codes, tokens credentials another destination. options(shinyOAuth.max_body_bytes = 1048576) - maximum response size (default 1 MiB) package requests connection calls. perform_resource_req() applies prepared requests well URLs.

title: Package options reference

Configure workers first, shown Usage. options(shinyOAuth.async_timeout = 10000) – per-task timeout milliseconds mirai async tasks. using mirai dispatcher (default), timed-tasks automatically cancelled resolve mirai error. Use NULL (default) timeout, whole number 0 2147483647. Ignored falling back ‘future’ backend

title: Package options reference

title: Package options reference
text: providers omit token lifetime. fallback lets ordinary OAuth clients track expiry case. options(shinyOAuth.default_expires_in = 3600) – fallback token lifetime (seconds) provider omits expires_in token response

title: Package options reference
text: settings control token responses addresses app accepts. options(shinyOAuth.access_token_cnf = "opaque") – use "opaque" avoid decoding access-token binding data. compatibility default "jwt" reads cnf without signature verification. options(shinyOAuth.leeway = 30) – default clock skew leeway (seconds) ID token exp/iat/nbf checks state payload issued_at future check options(shinyOAuth.max_id_token_lifetime = 86400) – maximum ID token lifetime seconds (exp - iat). additional package check beyond OIDC expiry check. Default 86400 (24 hours). Set Inf disable check options(shinyOAuth.allowed_non_https_hosts = c("localhost", "127.0.0.1", "::1", "[::1]")) - allows hosts use http:// non-OIDC URL checks; relax OIDC discovery options(shinyOAuth.allow_insecure_oidc_loopback = TRUE) – development-opt-OIDC issuer endpoint URLs HTTP loopback origins; production OIDC metadata URLs must use HTTPS options(shinyOAuth.allowed_hosts = c()) – non-empty, restricts accepted hosts list options(shinyOAuth.allow_hs = TRUE) – opt‑HMAC validation ID tokens (HS256/HS384/HS512). Requires strictly server‑side client_secret exactly one HS algorithm id_token_allowed_algs, binding shared key one algorithm (RFC 8725 section 3.1) options(shinyOAuth.client_assertion_ttl = 120L) – lifetime seconds JWT client assertions used client_secret_jwt private_key_jwt token endpoint authentication. Finite values 60 seconds coerced 60 seconds, finite values 300 seconds clamped 300 seconds, NA non-finite values fall back 120-second default options(shinyOAuth.state_fail_delay_ms = 0) – delay state-validation failures, milliseconds. Default 0 adds delay; one positive number sets fixed delay, two set random bounds. Positive delays block R even async = TRUE; add timing noise rather constant-time validation. allowed_hosts patterns support globs (*, ?). example, c(".example.com") matches domain subdomains; "*" accepts host.

}, error = function(e) NULL)     list(connection_id = connection[["id"]], revision = context[["revision"]], data = data)   })    output[["patient"]] <- renderText({     connection <- title: OAuth 2.0 / OAuth 2.1 implementation decisions
text: Pin OAuth 2.1 draft 16, published 2026-09-03; remains Internet-Draft. Sections 1.8 10 support dual-version operation. Section 4.1.1 requires S256 rather plain; §7.5.1.1’s -PKCE exception requires confidential client server assurance proper OIDC nonce use deployment request. Unknown assurance remains unknown. Sections 1.5, 1.7.1 5 respectively govern transport, recommended capacity token transport. Keep token request’s existing redirect_uri compatibility (§10.2). Assess code/refresh, enabled PAR applicable identity retrieval; report optional introspection/revocation separately unless requested assessment context. Future arbitrary resource URLs, server refresh replay policy, browser TLS, registered redirect matching deployment secret custody remain external evidence. Reuse existing topology (authorization_server_mode), nonce, identity, state extension policies. Manual OAuth-providers need invented OIDC metadata requirement. OIDC Core RFC 9700 remain relevant identity deployment responsibilities. checker must avoid endpoint_auth_client() S7 validation can probe signing capability; extract pure effective-settings resolver necessary. Async capture already covers shinyOAuth.*; verify clearing absent values reused workers bind effective transport policy pending transactions.

code: # Replace this example provider and client ID with your registered application. provider <- oauth_provider(   name = "Example service",   auth_url = "https://example.com/authorize",   token_url = "https://example.com/token",   token_auth_style = "public" ) client <- oauth_client(   provider = provider,   client_id = "example-client",   redirect_uri = "http://127.0.0.1:8100/callback/service",   resource_bases = c(api = "https://api.example.com") )  # Create the manager once, outside server(). # Register http://127.0.0.1:8100 as the GitHub OAuth App callback URL. if (   # Example requires configured GitHub OAuth 2.0 app   # (go to https://github.com/settings/developers to create one):   nzchar(Sys.getenv("GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID")) &&     nzchar(Sys.getenv("GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET")) &&     interactive() ) {   library(shiny)   library(shinyOAuth)    # Define client   client <- oauth_client(     provider = oauth_provider_github(),     client_id = Sys.getenv("GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID"),     client_secret = Sys.getenv("GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET"),     redirect_uri = "http://127.0.0.1:8100",     scopes = c("read:user", "user:email")   )    # Choose which app you want to run   app_to_run <- NULL   while (!isTRUE(app_to_run %in% c(1:4))) {     app_to_run <- readline(       prompt = paste0(         "Which example app do you want to run?
",         "  1: Auto-redirect login
",         "  2: Manual login button
",         "  3: Fetch additional resource with access token
",         "  4: No app (all will be defined but none run)
",         "Enter 1, 2, 3, or 4... "       )     )   }    if (app_to_run %in% c(1:3)) {     cli::cli_alert_info(paste0(       "Will run example app {app_to_run} on {.url http://127.0.0.1:8100}
",       "Open this URL in a regular browser (viewers in RStudio/Positron/etc. ",       "cannot perform necessary redirects)"     ))   }    # Example app with auto-redirect (1) -----------------------------------------    ui_1 <- oauth_ui(     fluidPage(       uiOutput("login")     ),     id = "auth",     client = client   )    server_1 <- function(input, output, session) {     # Auto-redirect (default):     auth <- oauth_module_server(       "auth",       client,       auto_redirect = TRUE     )      output[["login"]] <- renderUI({       if (auth[["authenticated"]]) {         user_info <- auth[["token"]]@userinfo         tagList(           tags[["p"]]("You are logged in!"),           tags[["pre"]](paste(capture.output(str(user_info)), collapse = "
"))         )       } else {         tags[["p"]]("You are not logged in.")       }     })   }    app_1 <- shinyApp(ui_1, server_1)   if (app_to_run == "1") {     runApp(       app_1,       port = 8100,       launch.browser = FALSE     )   }    # Example app with manual login button (2) -----------------------------------    ui_2 <- oauth_ui(     fluidPage(       actionButton("login_btn", "Login"),       actionButton("logout_btn", "Logout"),       uiOutput("login")     ),     id = "auth",     client = client   )    server_2 <- function(input, output, session) {     auth <- oauth_module_server(       "auth",       client,       auto_redirect = FALSE     )      observeEvent(input[["login_btn"]], {       auth[["request_login"]]()     })     observeEvent(input[["logout_btn"]], {       auth[["logout"]]()     })      output[["login"]] <- renderUI({       if (auth[["authenticated"]]) {         user_info <- auth[["token"]]@userinfo         tagList(           tags[["p"]]("You are logged in!"),           tags[["pre"]](paste(capture.output(str(user_info)), collapse = "
"))         )       } else {         tags[["p"]]("You are not logged in.")       }     })   }    app_2 <- shinyApp(ui_2, server_2)   if (app_to_run == "2") {     runApp(       app_2,       port = 8100,       launch.browser = FALSE     )   }    # Example app requesting additional resource with access token (3) -----------    # Below app shows the authenticated username + their GitHub repositories,   # fetched via GitHub API using the access token obtained during login    ui_3 <- oauth_ui(     fluidPage(       uiOutput("ui")     ),     id = "auth",     client = client   )    server_3 <- function(input, output, session) {     auth <- oauth_module_server(       "auth",       client,       auto_redirect = TRUE     )      repositories <- reactiveVal(NULL)     repository_error <- reactiveVal(FALSE)      observe({       req(auth[["authenticated"]])        # Example additional API request using the access token       # (e.g., fetch user repositories from GitHub)       # This loads one page; use the API's pagination for further results.       repos_data <- tryCatch(         {           resp <- perform_resource_req(             auth[["token"]],             "https://api.github.com/user/repos",             query = list(per_page = 30)           )           httr2::resp_check_status(resp)           httr2::resp_body_json(resp, simplifyVector = TRUE)         },         error = function(e) NULL       )        repository_error(is.null(repos_data))       repositories(repos_data)     })      # Render username + their repositories     output[["ui"]] <- renderUI({       if (isTRUE(auth[["authenticated"]])) {         user_info <- auth[["token"]]@userinfo         repos <- repositories()          return(tagList(           tags[["p"]](paste("You are logged in as:", user_info[["login"]])),           tags[["h4"]]("Your repositories:"),           if (repository_error()) {             tags[["p"]]("Could not load repositories.")           } else if (!is.null(repos) && length(repos) == 0) {             tags[["p"]]("No repositories returned.")           } else if (!is.null(repos)) {             tags[["ul"]](               Map(                 function(url, name) {                   # Render names as text; accept only GitHub HTTPS links.                   if (isTRUE(grepl("^https://github\.com/", url))) {                     tags[["li"]](tags[["a"]](                       href = url,                       target = "_blank",                       rel = "noopener noreferrer",                       name                     ))                   } else {                     tags[["li"]](name)                   }                 },                 repos[["html_url"]],                 repos[["full_name"]]               )             )           } else {             tags[["p"]]("Loading repositories...")           }         ))       }        return(tags[["p"]]("You are not logged in."))     })   }    app_3 <- shinyApp(ui_3, server_3)   if (app_to_run == "3") {     runApp(       app_3,       port = 8100,       launch.browser = FALSE     )   } }

code:
if (   # Example requires configured Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) tenant:   nzchar(Sys.getenv("MS_TENANT")) &&     interactive() &&     requireNamespace("later", quietly = TRUE) ) {   library(shiny)   library(shinyOAuth)    # Configure provider and client (Microsoft Entra ID with your tenant)   client <- oauth_client(     provider = oauth_provider_microsoft(       # Provide your own tenant ID here (set as environment variable MS_TENANT)       tenant = Sys.getenv("MS_TENANT")     ),     # Azure CLI public-client app ID; the tenant must permit this app.     # For your deployed app, use your own registration and redirect URI:     client_id = "04b07795-8ddb-461a-bbee-02f9e1bf7b46",     client_secret = "",     redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8100",     scopes = c("openid", "profile", "email")   )    # UI   ui <- oauth_ui(     fluidPage(       h3("OAuth demo (Microsoft Entra ID)"),       uiOutput("oauth_error"),       tags[["hr"]](),       h4("Auth object (summary)"),       verbatimTextOutput("auth_print"),       tags[["hr"]](),       h4("User info"),       verbatimTextOutput("user_info")     ),     id = "auth",     client = client   )    # Server   server <- function(input, output, session) {     auth <- oauth_module_server("auth", client)      output[["auth_print"]] <- renderText({       authenticated <- auth[["authenticated"]]       tok <- auth[["token"]]       err <- auth[["error"]]        paste0(         "Authenticated?",         if (isTRUE(authenticated)) " YES" else " NO",         "
",         "Has token? ",         if (!is.null(tok)) "YES" else "NO",         "
",         "Has error? ",         if (!is.null(err)) "YES" else "NO",         "

",         "Token present: ",         !is.null(tok),         "
",         "Has refresh token: ",         !is.null(tok) && isTRUE(nzchar(tok@refresh_token)),         "
",         "Has ID token: ",         !is.null(tok) && !is.na(tok@id_token),         "
",         "Expires at: ",         if (!is.null(tok)) tok@expires_at else "N/A"       )     })      output[["user_info"]] <- renderPrint({       req(auth[["authenticated"]])       auth[["token"]]@userinfo     })      observeEvent(       list(auth[["error"]], auth[["error_description"]]),       {         if (interactive() && !is.null(auth[["error_description"]])) {           rlang::inform(c(             "OAuth error details",             "i" = paste0("error: ", auth[["error"]]),             "i" = paste0("error_description: ", auth[["error_description"]])           ))         }       },       ignoreInit = TRUE     )      output[["oauth_error"]] <- renderUI({       if (is.null(auth[["error"]])) {         return(NULL)       }        msg <- if (identical(auth[["error"]], "access_denied")) {         "Sign-in was canceled or denied. Please try again."       } else {         "Authentication failed. Please try again."       }        div(class = "alert alert-danger", role = "alert", msg)     })   }    # Open localhost:8100 to match the Azure CLI app's registered redirect URI   # and keep browser cookies on the same host. Schedule the browser launch   # before runApp() starts blocking R.   later::later(     function() {       utils::browseURL("http://localhost:8100")     },     delay = 0.25   )    # Run app   runApp(shinyApp(ui, server), port = 8100, launch.browser = FALSE) }

code: # Configure generic OAuth 2.0 provider (no OIDC) generic_provider <- oauth_provider(   name = "example",   auth_url = "https://example.com/oauth/authorize",   token_url = "https://example.com/oauth/token",   # Optional URL for fetching user info:   userinfo_url = "https://example.com/oauth/userinfo" )  # Configure generic OIDC provider manually # (This defaults to using nonce & ID token validation) generic_oidc_provider <- oauth_provider_oidc(   name = "My OIDC",   base_url = "https://my-issuer.example.com" )  # Look up an OIDC provider's settings with discovery # (requires network access) if (interactive()) {   # Using Auth0 sample issuer as an example   oidc_discovery_provider <- oauth_provider_oidc_discover(     issuer = "https://samples.auth0.com/"   ) }  # GitHub preconfigured provider github_provider <- oauth_provider_github()  # Google preconfigured provider google_provider <- oauth_provider_google()  # Microsoft preconfigured provider # For a complete app using a custom tenant ID, see: # https://lukakoning.github.io/shinyOAuth/reference/oauth_provider_microsoft.html  # Spotify preconfigured provider spotify_provider <- oauth_provider_spotify()  # Slack via OIDC discovery # (requires network access) if (interactive()) {   slack_provider <- oauth_provider_slack() }  # Keycloak # (requires configured Keycloak realm; example below is therefore not run) if (interactive()) {   options(shinyOAuth.allow_insecure_oidc_loopback = TRUE)   oauth_provider_keycloak(base_url = "http://localhost:8080", realm = "myrealm") }  # Auth0 # (requires configured Auth0 domain; example below is therefore not run) if (interactive()) {   oauth_provider_auth0(domain = "your-tenant.auth0.com") }  # Okta # (requires configured Okta domain; example below is therefore not run) if (interactive()) {   oauth_provider_okta(domain = "dev-123456.okta.com") }

title: Discover and create an OpenID Connect (OIDC) OAuthProvider — oauth_provider_oidc_discover
text: issuer OIDC issuer base URL (including scheme), e.g., "https://login.example.com". standard discovery-document URL ending /.well-known/openid-configuration also accepted. discovered issuer must map back metadata location; exact returned issuer, including trailing slash, retained subsequent validation. name Optional friendly provider name. Defaults issuer hostname use_pkce Logical, whether use PKCE provider. Defaults TRUE. Public clients require PKCE. Setting FALSE also prevents automatic selection public-client authentication; confidential-client method must available explicitly configured instead. use_nonce Logical, whether use OIDC nonce. Defaults TRUE id_token_validation Logical, whether validate ID tokens automatically provider. Defaults TRUE token_auth_style Authentication style token requests: "header" (client_secret_basic), "body" (client_secret_post), "public" (public client; send client_id ). alias "none" also accepted "public". NULL (default), inferred conservatively discovery: "header" (client_secret_basic) preferred, followed "body" (client_secret_post), "public" none advertised PKCE enabled. Set token_auth_style = "public" explicitly public client registration. JWT methods ("client_secret_jwt", "private_key_jwt") mTLS methods ("tls_client_auth", "self_signed_tls_client_auth") must selected explicitly. title: shinyOAuth 0.7.0
text: Use Shiny login R packages: oauth_module_server() now provides connection(). Connections module oauth_connections_server() offer $access_token() obtain current bearer token, refreshing needed. $has_scopes() helps apps enable features based available permissions, showing edit button write access. $request(refresh = TRUE) reduces failures expired tokens refreshing API call, without replaying token-expiry error. See vignette("external-integrations", package = "shinyOAuth") (online guide) examples. Exported tokens retain provider’s permissions, can broader app’s local limits. Access several APIs, calendars contacts, one login: Configure token_targets oauth_client() providers supporting RFC 8707 resource indicators Microsoft token acquisition. API can token; select one , example, connection$access_token(target = "calendar"). token targets, set reauth_after_seconds app needs time-limited login; API token expiry alone need end local login. See vignette("token-targets", package = "shinyOAuth") (online guide). Provider helpers compatibility improvements: Added helpers ORCID, GitLab, Amazon Cognito, Globus Auth, Hugging Face, SURFconext, authentik, reducing manual provider configuration. Microsoft sign-can skip Graph profile retrieval oauth_provider_microsoft(userinfo_required = FALSE) token intended another API. avoids failed profile request without disabling OIDC identity checks. oauth_provider_oidc() preserves exact issuer URLs, including trailing slashes, accepts separate issuer differs endpoint base URL. Fixed GitHub’s permission-response format Microsoft directory-ID letter case. Ed25519 keys now work signed login requests self-signed mTLS registration. Fixed introspection revocation calls credentials authentication settings differ used token exchange. Improved compatibility upcoming S7 releases: avoided := import conflicts rlang warnings signing-algorithm default. Package load, unload build now use S7 lifecycle hooks available, retaining support older S7 releases. Updated base64url tests upcoming openssl releases, reject invalid base64 error instead returning empty bytes. fixes test failure; existing JWT, JWK encrypted-state validation already handles decoding failures. reliable sign-connection management: oauth_module_server() adds reauthorize(), oauth_connections_server() adds reauthorize(connection_id), “sign ” flow preserves previously reduced permissions. Repeated denied logins longer build cookies block later attempts. Retained browser sessions recover returning another website, simultaneous login responses longer displace pending logins. Stale responses discarded logout replacement login. Improved cleanup rejected logins refreshes. revoke_on_session_end = TRUE also attempts provider revocation expiry maximum login age ends local access, reducing tokens left active. Encrypted login state now preserves Unicode text non-UTF-8 locales rejects malformed UTF-8 JSON parsing. Connection polling SMART permission checks avoid repeated work, reducing background overhead apps many saved connections. Safer API requests identity checks: Package HTTPS requests now require TLS 1.2 later default, providing minimum across R installations. Protocol JSON now uses jsonlite::parse_json() instead fromJSON(). Responses state envelopes parsed literal JSON text, preventing URL-like file-path input triggering server-side request forgery (SSRF) unintended local-file reads. Stricter checks catch malformed provider responses configuration mistakes. Reusing RSA key HMAC secret conflicting signing algorithms rejected; use separate keys secrets different algorithms required. Numeric OIDC claim requirements longer rounded reaching provider, including signed authorization requests. Single-element values vectors remain JSON arrays automatically. Invalid claims requests rejected configuring client. Manual get_userinfo() calls apply configured identity signature checks even automatic retrieval disabled. Pass complete OAuthToken profile can checked signed-user. DPoP signing now matches URL actually sent, fixing failures internationalized URLs normalized paths. DPoP requests reject automatic redirects, unsafe request overrides rejected. Resource URL inputs limited 8192 bytes, including query parameters. Input limits leaner parsing reduce worker slowdowns oversized malformed callbacks provider responses. Improved log trace redaction reduces exposure private URL paths, query parameters, sensitive provider diagnostics. Deployment configuration changes: precise configuration checks help prevent logins saved connections resuming changed login policies. Older records invalidated: users must sign connect upgrading. Update workers sharing keys storage together. custom userinfo_id_selector uses settings outside function body, set userinfo_id_selector_policy_id update settings change. Discovery checks client authentication provider’s metadata. authentication methods omitted, HTTP Basic (token_auth_style = "header") assumed. Use manual provider configuration services require different method without declaring . Enforcing UserInfo claim requirements now requires automatic profile retrieval: set userinfo_required = TRUE configure userinfo_url provider. prevents login silently skipping requested profile checks. Custom form-post stores now require atomic set_if_absent addition take, simultaneous callbacks overwrite reuse pending records. Custom JWKS caches run synchronously unless declared safe separate R processes worker_safe = TRUE, avoiding reuse process-specific connections workers. See custom_cache(). Unsupported SMART OIDC reauth_after_seconds limits now fail startup. Use NULL indefinite_session = FALSE avoid later login failure. check_oauth21() reports uninspected mTLS credentials unresolved instead assuming configured files usable. Encrypted JARM callbacks now use temporary R process limit memory growth decryption failures. Deployments need callr >= 3.7.6 must allow R subprocesses; callbacks incur process startup time. Requires jsonlite >= 1.6 literal-text parse_json() parsing openssl >= 2.1.2 RSA-OAEP encryption/decryption used encrypted authorization requests (JAR) responses (JARM). future async backend requires promises >= 1.3.3 future_promise() can dispatch work newer versions future.

title: shinyOAuth 0.6.0
text: CRAN release: 2026-09-17 Added optional connections apps using one OAuth authorizations: oauth_connection() combines module’s current token client’s approved resource_bases required_scopes. $request() method uses refreshed credentials restricts calls APIs; status selected identity information available without exposing credentials. oauth_connections(), oauth_connections_ui() oauth_connections_server(), manages separate authorizations, including repeated logins provider. Connections normally end Shiny session; optional browser local-account retention restores navigation. oauth_connection_store_memory() stores encrypted credentials one R process. oauth_browser_owner() oauth_account_owner() configure can restore long. Retention survive R restarts. Managed $refresh(scopes = ...) can reduce permissions preserving required scopes. Later refreshes retain reduction; widening requires new authorization. Disconnect removes local access optional remote revocation. Refresh revocation account credentials shared across connections. callback_policy = "issuer" "shared_routes" permits shared callback URLs issuer validation; distinct routes remain default required encrypted JARM. Ordinary OAuth modules can share UI additional_clients. Added SMART FHIR STU 2.2 app support: smart_discover() reads metadata approved FHIR server; smart_client() combines existing public, secret-based, asymmetric app registration standalone EHR launch. checks server capabilities permissions, requires S256 PKCE TLS 1.2 newer, enables signed user identity requested. smart_launch_route() accepts EHR launches configured clients using browser retention. SMART supports direct authorization query form POST callbacks. smart_context() reports current patient, encounter, validated user reference, revision detecting context changes refresh. smart_patient() smart_fhir_user() fetch corresponding FHIR resources authorized within configured server. Required permissions remain enforced reduced grants refreshes. Offline access negotiation requires opt-. Token responses must supply scopes positive lifetime; initial_expires_in_fallback can provide explicit fallback initial response. OAuthToken exposes additional token response parameters extra_fields. successful refresh replaces list; initial_extra_fields preserves initial response. retain nested values explicit nulls redacted printed. Added oauth_ui() handle URL-based callbacks app UI loads. Wrap UI id client used oauth_module_server(). oauth_ui() oauth_form_post_ui() accept named client registries apps using multiple OAuth modules providers. Added check_oauth21(), read-assessment client provider configuration OAuth 2.1 draft 16. reports configuration problems, external prerequisites, recommendations without making requests changing settings, including effective TLS policy SMART clients. Browser bindings isolated origin, tab, login, app/module stay URLs bookmarks. Callbacks enforce registered path response transport, preserve escaped paths, reject oversized input routing. Shared callback state encrypted requires atomic storage. oauth_form_post_ui() supports trusted-proxy URI resolution. New visitors evict retained connections browsers pending authorizations. Added signed encrypted authorization responses (JARM) response_mode = "jwt", "query.jwt", "form_post.jwt" oauth_module_server(). Algorithms can configured discovered; jarm_max_lifetime defaults 600 seconds. Malformed claims headers rejected. handle_callback() continues accept classic callbacks. authorization_server_mode supports multiple authorization servers validated issuer responses distinct registered callback routes. compare_callback_issuer can check supplied issuer without requiring older providers send one; required issuer JARM checks remain enforced. Function argument names consistent. CRAN 0.5.0 argument names positions remain supported, existing S7 property names: Login, token, userinfo, resource-request, mTLS registration helpers consistently accept client token. handle_callback() accepts callback state state; introspection revocation helpers select access refresh tokens token_kind. Provider constructors discovery use id_token_allowed_algs ID-token signing algorithms. Clients use introspection_checks extra introspection requirements. Client assertion keys, mTLS, Request Object, JARM settings use client_assertion_*, mtls_*, request_object_*, jarm_* names. See ?oauth_client ?oauth_provider current arguments. oauth_module_server() uses refresh_check_interval_ms make polling interval’s millisecond unit explicit. Client provider configuration changes: Client credentials longer default OAUTH_CLIENT_ID OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET; omitted secret treated absent. Public clients must use PKCE. Printed objects redact credentials sensitive URL components. endpoint_auth configures authentication separately PAR, introspection, revocation, including credentials, assertions, mTLS, headers. Discovered authentication methods algorithms negotiated per endpoint. client_assertion_typ supports JWT client-authentication+jwt, including per-endpoint overrides. Low-level S7 constructors use OIDC DPoP security defaults helper constructors reject malformed security assurance settings. Provider configuration changes: infer_oidc_from_issuer = FALSE allows generic OAuth issuer validation without enabling OIDC; default remains TRUE. explicit jwks_uri overrides discovery across signing-key consumers. Missing disallowed required key locations fail configuration. userinfo_allowed_algs configures signed UserInfo algorithms independently ID-token algorithms, corresponding discovery support. allow_missing_token_type = TRUE explicitly permits Bearer-providers omit required token type. default remains strict; fallback apply DPoP clients replace invalid values. Provider helper updates: Added oauth_provider_apple() oauth_client_secret_apple() Apple sign-. Validated Apple email_verified strings become logical values, including claim checks id_token_claims. oauth_provider_microsoft() rejects unrecognized tenants instead silently disabling OIDC. Use directory GUID supported tenant alias; OAuth-operation requires explicit id_token_validation = FALSE. oauth_provider_slack(profile = ...) supports "confidential" "public_pkce" registrations. Spotify uses immutable account_id. Migrate stored id mappings audit digests authenticated profile; allow_legacy_id = TRUE permits temporary fallback account_id absent. Okta’s org server supported, Auth0’s trailing-slash issuer preserved, oauth_provider_oidc() respects authentication-style override. OIDC discovery accepts issuer standard discovery URL, preserves exact issuer endpoint paths, requires exact issuer match. Required metadata URL syntax validated; optional capability arrays may empty null malformed. HTTPS required unless shinyOAuth.allow_insecure_oidc_loopback = TRUE permits loopback development. Endpoints may use hosts subject shinyOAuth.allowed_hosts; JWKS retains separate host policy. Transport failures identify attempted discovery URL underlying error. JWKS handling rejects malformed keys inconsistent key usage, allowing unrelated public extensions. Discovery preserves escaped issuer paths enforces current host pinning policies. Caching respects HTTP freshness -store directives; rotation works provider reuses key ID. RSA keys require least 2048 bits trusted algorithm choice: unlabelled keys use RS256 unless single RSA algorithm configured. Generic OAuth discovery can fall back OIDC discovery locations. Ed25519 keys support EdDSA Ed25519 verification, client assertions, Request Objects, DPoP. Outbound RSA signing also supports explicitly selected RS384; RS256 remains default. OIDC claim validation consistently checks standard optional claim types ID tokens UserInfo, including refreshed nonces. UserInfo must match validated ID token’s sub; additional audiences require explicit trust multiple audiences require correct azp. Future authentication times rejected, requested claim objects compare independently member order. JSON profile arrays retain existing vector data-frame structure. Authentication deadlines extended refresh. Token lifetimes calculated conservatively, long lifetimes future timestamps avoid integer overflow; invalid lifetime settings rejected. Concurrent refreshes combined, stale results ignored, login ID token remains continuity baseline. Refresh credentials retired potentially consuming failures. Ordinary OAuth refreshes explicitly request known retained scopes earlier reductions preserved. DPoP-bound tokens, including opaque tokens, work consistently UserInfo resource helpers downgraded Bearer. Proofs preserve actual request path, retries use fresh nonces intermediate responses. nonce limit defaults 4096 bytes, configurable shinyOAuth.dpop_nonce_max_bytes; oversized responses report clear error. Malformed conflicting token-binding thumbprints rejected. Authorization request, JAR, PAR improvements: authorization_method = "POST" supports long browser requests provider supports ; SMART requires advertised authorize-post. Shiny submits form automatically. prepare_authorization_request() returns URL, method, form fields custom browser navigation. Authorization URLs reject conflicting repeated managed parameters preserving valid fixed queries repeated resource indicators. Configure policy scopes max_age client properties extra_auth_params, endpoint URL; policy applies across transports. Hosted Request Objects use HTTPS one-time handles oauth_ui(). Encryption accepts public PEM keys honors key metadata, size, pins, one refresh key-selection failure hardened decryption checks. PAR avoids generic retries duplicate authorization requests; bounded DPoP nonce retries remain available. mTLS improvements: mtls_require_observed_cnf defaults TRUE. server-enforced opaque tokens, keep mtls_certificate_bound_access_tokens = TRUE set FALSE; observed binding must still match. Certificate chains must leaf-first. Registration validates subject/SAN identifiers, issuer ordering, IPv6 SANs, HTTPS registration key URLs. Certificate rotation longer causes unbounded cache growth. Unsupported PEM-based mTLS Windows Schannel reports targeted error. Token, introspection, HTTP handling validates credentials, media types, response sizes, activity, scopes use. Form encoding consistent, supported parameter overrides replace existing values. Resource helpers preserve escaped paths adding queries, reject competing credentials inherited authentication/cache/retry policies, support per-call resource_hosts. Method-changing curl options HEAD requests bodies rejected prevent unsafe retries incorrect DPoP proofs; configure methods httr2::req_method(). Retries honor bounded Retry-values. Invalid numeric retry/assertion options use safe defaults, URL-check flags must logical. shinyOAuth.tls_min_version can require TLS 1.2 1.3 across package requests async workers. Audit OpenTelemetry output safer default: Conditions, displays, hooks, exports redact bound sensitive provider data, URLs, header parameters. Unknown OAuth errors become unknown; diagnostic text literal. Native hooks receive shiny_session$session_token_digest; raw tokens require shinyOAuth.audit_include_raw_session_token = TRUE. Authorization details require shinyOAuth.otel_include_authorization_details = TRUE. Configured audit digest keys require least 32 bytes; invalid values fail clearly. Callback rejection connection disconnect/revocation outcomes reported consistently. Cloud Run example uses pinned deployment dependencies. Spotify examples handle remote content safely fix playback formatting; dashboard installed examples/spotify-dashboard.R. Async use requires mirai >= 2.5.1; future_promise() fallback uses parallel-safe random-number generation.

title: shinyOAuth 0.5.0
text: CRAN release: 2026-05-23 Added mutual-TLS (‘mTLS’, RFC 8705) support, including mTLS client authentication, certificate-bound access tokens, mTLS endpoint aliases, exported oauth_client_mtls_registration() helper RFC 8705 client metadata. Added Demonstrating Proof--Possession (‘DPoP’, RFC 9449) support. Clients configured dpop_private_key now send DPoP proofs token protected-resource requests, include dpop_jkt authorization requests, can require token_type = "DPoP" plus cnf.jkt binding, replay one DPoP-Nonce challenge token protected-resource requests. Added JWT-Secured Authorization Request (‘JAR’, RFC 9101) support. oauth_client() can now send signed encrypted Request Objects via request_object_mode = "request" (sent parameter) via request_object_mode = "request_uri" (served Shiny app). Added Pushed Authorization Request (‘PAR’, RFC 9126) support. Providers can now configure par_url directly pick OIDC discovery, login flows push authorization request redirect returned request_uri. Added response_mode = "form_post" support authorization-code callbacks. Apps can wrap UI oauth_form_post_ui() Shiny accepts provider POST, stores callback server-side one-time handle, lets oauth_module_server() finish existing state, issuer, token exchange flow. Stored callback handles bounded effective state/store TTL shinyOAuth.callback_max_form_post_* size-cap options. Added OpenTelemetry (‘OTel’) support (using ‘otel’ package). ‘shinyOAuth’ now emits OTel logs existing audit events traces key OAuth operations module initialization, login/callback handling, token exchange/refresh, userinfo/introspection/revocation, session-end cleanup. See vignette("opentelemetry", package = "shinyOAuth") information. span catalog includes form-post callback state consumption documents opt-policy exception messages. Observability audit logging improvements: Improved observability correlation existing audit flows. Interactive login now reuses single flow trace_id across redirect issuance, callback validation, token exchange, login outcome events, making easier correlate pre-redirect post-redirect Shiny sessions single login round-trip; async work also carries accurate originating Shiny session/process context worker-emitted events. audit_login_success$sub_source = "id_token" now reflects OAuthToken@id_token_validated result returned token, telemetry longer overstates ID-token validation tests debug options skip signature verification. Sanitized HTTP audit context now redacts remote_addr well proxy headers, default audit events longer export raw client IP addresses. Improved existing audit event types. audit_token_exchange audit_token_refresh now include expires_in_synthesized, indicating provider return usable expires_in shinyOAuth synthesize one; audit_login_failed now distinguishes async payload-validation state-store-lookup failures async token-exchange failures; audit_userinfo distinguishes missing sub JWT/JWKS validation failures; error-state consumption events use logical state digest available better correlation. See vignette("audit-logging", package = "shinyOAuth") information. options(shinyOAuth.trace_hook = ...) longer treated separate documented event sink. Prefer options(shinyOAuth.audit_hook = ...); old trace_hook option now remains backward-compatible alias audit_hook unset. Removed documented global shinyOAuth.print_errors / shinyOAuth.print_traceback options. Internal console error logging now uses explicit internal flags instead package-wide option fallbacks. http_error audit events now omit raw provider oauth_error_description text default keep oauth_error, oauth_error_uri, body_digest. raw description emitted options(shinyOAuth.expose_error_body = TRUE) enabled debugging. err_http() now strips query strings, fragments, userinfo response URLs surfacing condition messages emitted events, reducing leakage authorization codes, state, request URIs, similar URL-borne secrets. oauth_module_server() now: Explicitly ignores new login requests session already authenticated. Fails cleanly startup revoke_on_session_end = TRUE provider expose revocation_url, instead crashing formatting configuration error. Applies browser-token double-submit check OAuth error callbacks , deferring ?error=... handling browser token available treating browser-token mismatches invalid_state instead surfacing provider-controlled error text. Forwards oauth_client(introspect = TRUE) proactive refresh path, proactive refresh now follows refresh-time token introspection policy direct refresh_token(..., introspect = TRUE) calls. Preserves invalid_state callback error state CSRF/state/browser-token validation failures instead flattening paths token_exchange_error. Drops provider error_uri values unless absolute HTTPS URLs, unsafe schemes like javascript: longer surfaced values$error_uri. Validates browser_cookie_path strictly, requiring leading / rejecting semicolons control characters unsafe cookie attributes injected configured cookie Path. OAuthToken OAuthClient now print redacted token/secret/key previews instead exposing full credential material default console output. OAuthToken now tracks normalized granted_scopes plus granted_scopes_verified, apps can distinguish scope sets explicitly returned ones carried forward provider omitted scope. Refresh now preserves prior granted scopes instead widening back client’s configured scopes refresh response omits scope. oauth_client() (OAuthClient) now: Accepts custom state-store entries omit unused pkce_code_verifier nonce fields provider require , still rejecting missing PKCE nonce values checks enabled. Supports enforce_callback_issuer = TRUE require RFC 9207 iss callback parameter shared-redirect multi-issuer deployments. Relatedly, handle_callback() now accepts iss, advanced callers building around prepare_call() can supply callback issuer get client-level RFC 9207 check token exchange. Auto-enables RFC 9207 callback issuer enforcement caller leaves enforce_callback_issuer unset provider advertises authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported = TRUE. native RFC 8707 resource support, authorization, token exchange, refresh requests can request audience-restricted tokens without dropping manual extra params. Defaults scope_validation "warn", RFC-compliant reduced grants surface warnings unless opt scope_validation = "strict". Warns list-based OIDC claims requests use single-element values entry without (...), jsonlite::toJSON(auto_unbox = TRUE) otherwise serialize OIDC array constraint scalar. Rejects impossible JOSE alg/private-key combinations JWT client assertions DPoP proofs emitting invalid JOSE headers. Also enforces OIDC claim request value values constraints claims_validation enabled, just presence essential = TRUE claims. Defaults enforceable OIDC claim requests claims_validation = "warn" callers request essential value-constrained claims set claims_validation explicitly, claim mismatches surfaced default unless callers opt claims_validation = "none". Carries effective requested scopes whole login flow. openid auto-added authorization request, sealed state payload, token-response scope validation, introspection scope validation now use effective scope set. Uses validated ID token sub introspect_elements = "sub" falling back userinfo, unvalidated ID token payloads longer anchor introspection subject check. Binds sealed callback state effective provider client security policy used redirect. Multi-worker deployments must now keep callback/login validation settings aligned across workers; otherwise callbacks fail fast invalid_state instead resuming different worker policy. oauth_provider() (OAuthProvider) now: Allows response_mode = "query" response_mode = "form_post" authorization-code callbacks, still rejecting unsupported modes "fragment". provider metadata advertises response_modes_supported, shinyOAuth also fails fast explicit response mode advertised. Treats nonce-enabled OIDC flows sufficient validation context userinfo_id_token_match, shinyOAuth now always binds userinfo validated ID token subject baseline exists. Raises typed shinyOAuth_input_error conditions malformed constructor inputs vector endpoint URLs empty discovery-helper domains, apps can trap provider validation failures consistently. Validates custom jwks_cache$get() signatures without calling cache construction, avoiding side effects duck-typed cache backends. Validates allowed_algs shinyOAuth’s actual inbound verifier support longer accepts RSA-PSS (PS256, PS384, PS512) entries, previously present generic helper’s defaults despite lacking verifier support. Older configs explicitly allowed algorithms must switch supported verifier algorithms. Reserves refresh_token parameter name extra_token_params prevent duplicate refresh-token parameters token refresh requests. oauth_provider_oidc_discover() now: Fails fast metadata advertises PKCE methods omits S256. shinyOAuth keeps S256 default allows downgrade plain pass pkce_method = "plain" explicitly. Fails fast discovery document omits jwks_uri selected policy still needs signing keys, including id_token_validation = TRUE, nonce-enabled OIDC flows, signed UserInfo JWT validation. misconfigurations now fail provider setup instead later JWKS fetch. Validates discovered jwks_uri values absolute-URL, scheme, host policy used discovery endpoints, invalid disallowed JWKS URLs now fail discovery instead later first JWKS fetch. Rejects issuer inputs contain query strings fragments building discovery URL, matching stricter issuer validation already used manually configured providers. Rejects non-scalar endpoint metadata values configuration error. Honors jwks_host_allow_only early jwks_uri host check, explicitly pinned cross-host JWKS endpoints longer require disabling issuer-host matching. Maps token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported = ["none"] distinct public token auth style never sends client_secret, even oauth_client() picks one OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET. oauth_provider_oidc() now trims trailing slashes base_url deriving endpoint URLs configured issuer, avoiding valid ID tokens rejected strict OIDC iss comparison helper configured URL like https://issuer.example/. oauth_provider_microsoft() longer drops Microsoft alias tenants OAuth 2.0 plus userinfo identity default. common organizations now validate ID tokens using Microsoft’s tenant-independent issuer signing-key issuer rules, consumers now validates stable consumer tenant issuer. validate_id_token() now properly rejects auth_time claims set future (beyond leeway). Previously, future auth_time produced negative elapsed value always passed max_age freshness check. introspect_token() now uses provider@userinfo_id_selector consistently checks authenticated subject fetched UserInfo data, now fails closed malformed introspection JSON. Non-object responses rejected instead normalized first parsed element. refresh_token() now: Refuses update userinfo unless can verify refreshed identity new preserved ID token subject, preventing identity confusion providers omit id_token refresh responses. called introspect = TRUE, enforces token introspection hard policy check instead best-effort metadata enrichment. Refresh now fails introspection unsupported, inactive, malformed, missing required introspect_elements sub, client_id, scope. get_userinfo() now: Applies hard JWK alg compatibility checks signed UserInfo JWT verification ID token verification, rejecting JWKS keys advertise different algorithm even signature verification otherwise succeed. Always requires non-empty sub claim userinfo responses OIDC providers (issuer configured), per OIDC Core section 5.3. Previously, non-compliant response without sub accepted userinfo_id_token_match enabled. signed-JWT path (validate_signed_userinfo_claims()) also now checks sub alongside existing iss/aud validation. Signed UserInfo JWT validation now: Enforces exp, iat, nbf temporal claims present, rejecting expired -yet-valid UserInfo JWT responses instead accepting based signature/issuer/audience. oauth_client() can also require specific UserInfo JWT temporal claims present via userinfo_jwt_required_time_claims. Uses internal JWS verifier instead jose::jwt_decode_sig(), EdDSA UserInfo JWTs can verify correctly, provider leeway honored consistently, invalid typ headers rejected. Successful token refresh responses now always require token_type, even allowed_token_types = character(). empty allowlist still disables value allowlisting, longer waives RFC-required field. Refreshed OIDC ID tokens now enforce full continuity auth_time, refresh-time nonce, azp addition existing iss / sub / aud checks. Token exchange refresh requests longer retry transport errors transient HTTP statuses (408/429/5xx). Authorization codes single-use refresh tokens may rotated use; retrying server already committed first request replay invalidated credential, causing invalid_grant errors triggering refresh-token replay detection. Hardened runtime JWKS discovery validating discovery issuer trusting jwks_uri. policy now stored OAuthProvider via issuer_match, provider discovery runtime JWKS fetches apply rule: url exact issuer URL matching, host scheme--host matching, none skip discovery issuer check. JWKS caching now respects global host policy immediately. Cached entries scoped current allowed_hosts / allowed_non_https_hosts settings, cache hits re-check stored jwks_uri JWKS trusted. Scope validation now treats omitted scope initial token response unchanged requested scope, matching RFC 6749 section 5.1 instead rejecting otherwise compliant authorization servers default. Strict token-response introspection scope validation now treats commas part single scope token, matching RFC 6749 instead splitting scope = "read,write" separate read write scopes. Missing expires_in values now default finite 3600-second fallback rather effectively indefinite session. Override options(shinyOAuth.default_expires_in = <seconds>), use oauth_module_server(reauth_after_seconds = ...) need stricter session-age cap. err_http() now guards oversized HTTP error bodies hashing JSON parsing, large chunked misleading error responses now trip existing body-size limit consistently. at_hash validation now resolves EdDSA verified signing key/JWK instead guessing alg alone: Ed25519 uses exact SHA-512 mapping, signature-skipped currently unsupported EdDSA curves fail closed. Deprecated error_on_softened(). remains narrow guard dev/debug softeners, docs now stop presenting comprehensive deployment-hardening check show explicit option checks instead. Renamed resource-request helpers resource_req() perform_resource_req(). existing public client_bearer_req() name remains available deprecated alias, perform_client_bearer_req() also exported deprecated compatibility alias. perform_resource_req() new function builds performs authenticated resource-request , DPoP-bound access tokens, replays one use_dpop_nonce challenge server-provided nonce. can also take pre-existing ‘httr2’ request objects layer authentication DPoP top.

title: shinyOAuth 0.4.0
text: CRAN release: 2026-02-14 ‘mirai’ & async backend improvements: Warnings messages emitted async workers (e.g., missing expires_in token response) now captured re-emitted main process appear R console. includes conditions user-supplied trace_hook / audit_hook functions: warnings, messages, errors (surfaced warnings) propagate back main thread. Replay can disabled via options(shinyOAuth.replay_async_conditions = FALSE). Async callback flow longer serializes full client object (including potentially non-serializable custom state_store / JWKS cache backends) worker context. state_store (already consumed main thread) replaced lightweight serializable dummy dispatch. client still fails serialization, flow falls back synchronous execution explicit warning instead opaque runtime error. reduced serialization overhead towards async workers using certain functions package namespace directly. Detect active daemons via mirai::daemons_set() instead mirai::status(). Falls back mirai::info() older ‘mirai’ versions lack mirai::daemons_set() (< 2.3.0). Configurable per-task timeout via options(shinyOAuth.async_timeout) (milliseconds); timed-‘mirai’ tasks automatically cancelled dispatcher. Default NULL (timeout). Async audit events now include mirai_error_type field. classifies mirai transport-level failures separately application-level errors. Prevent ‘mirai’ warning spam ‘stats’ maybe available workers. ID token validation (validate_id_token()): Now enforces RFC 7515 section 4.1.11 critical header parameter (crit) processing rules. Tokens containing unsupported critical extensions rejected shinyOAuth_id_token_error. current implementation supports critical extensions, crit presence triggers rejection. Now validates at_hash (Access Token hash) claim present ID token (per OIDC Core section 3.1.3.8 3.2.2.9). claim exists, access token binding verified; mismatch raises shinyOAuth_id_token_error. New id_token_at_hash_required property OAuthProvider (default FALSE) forces login fail ID token contain at_hash claim. Now validates, refreshed ID tokens, per OIDC Core section 12.2, iss aud claims original ID token’s values (just provider configuration) cover edge cases multi-tenant providers rotating issuer URIs. Enforced validated non-validated code paths. Now detects encrypted ID tokens (JWE compact serialization, 5 dot-separated segments) early raises clear shinyOAuth_id_token_error instead letting confusing alg/typ/parse failure propagate. Now validates auth_time claim max_age present extra_auth_params (OIDC Core section 3.1.2.1). Now enforces package-defined maximum ID token lifetime (exp - iat); tokens unreasonably long lifetimes rejected shinyOAuth_id_token_error. Configure via options(shinyOAuth.max_id_token_lifetime = <seconds>) (default 86400 24 hours). Set Inf disable check. Stricter state store usage: custom_cache() gains optional take parameter atomic get--delete. state_store_get_remove() prefers $take() available; falls back $get() + $remove() mandatory post-removal absence check (instead trusting $remove() return values). Non-cachem::cache_mem() stores without $take() now error default prevent TOCTOU replay attacks shared/multi-worker deployments. bypass error, operators must explicitly acknowledge risk setting options(shinyOAuth.allow_non_atomic_state_store = TRUE), downgrades error warning. OAuthClient validator now validates $take() signature present. $remove() return value longer relied upon fallback path; post-removal $get() absence check authoritative. Stricter JWKS cache handling: JWKS cache key now includes host-policy fields (jwks_host_issuer_match, jwks_host_allow_only). Previously, two provider configs issuer different host policies shared cache entry, allowing relaxed-policy provider populate cache strict-policy provider skip host validation cache hit. Cache entries now also store JWKS source host re-validate current provider policy read (defense--depth). Stricter URL validation: OAuthClient now rejects redirect URIs containing fragments (per RFC 6749, section 3.1.2); OAuthProvider now rejects issuer identifiers containing query fragment components, covering oauth_provider_oidc_discover() manual construction providers. Stricter state payload parsing: callback state now rejects embedded NUL bytes JSON decoding. Stricter response size validation: enforce max response body size outbound HTTP endpoints (token, introspection, userinfo, OIDC discovery, JWKS). Curl aborts transfer early Content-Length exceeds limit; post-download guard catches chunked responses. Default 1 MiB, configurable via options(shinyOAuth.max_body_bytes). OAuthProvider (S7 class): leeway validator now rejects non-finite values (Inf, -Inf, NaN). Previously passed validation silently coerced 0 runtime, effectively disabling clock-skew tolerance. Reserved OAuth parameter blocking extra_auth_params extra_token_params now case-insensitive trims whitespace. Vector inputs pkce_method URL parameters (auth_url, token_url, userinfo_url, introspection_url, revocation_url) now produce clear scalar-input errors instead cryptic coercion failures. OAuthClient (S7 class): Gains claims_validation property; client sends structured claims request parameter essential = TRUE entries, setting controls whether returned ID token /userinfo response checked essential claims (similar scope_validation). Gains required_acr_values property; enables client-side enforcement OIDC acr (Authentication Context Class Reference) claim. extra_token_headers now consistently applied revoke introspect requests, matching existing behavior token exchange refresh. Previously, provider integrations requiring custom headers across token endpoints partially fail revocation/introspection. Fixed incorrect warning client created Shiny case. Malformed client_assertion_alg client_assertion_audience values (e.g., character(0), multi-element vectors) now produce clear validation errors instead crashing base R subscript---bounds errors. Empty string "" client_assertion_audience now explicitly rejected instead silently treated “provided”. OAuthToken (S7 class): Gains read-id_token_claims property exposes decoded ID token JWT payload named list, surfacing OIDC claims (e.g., acr, amr, auth_time) without manual decoding. Gains id_token_validated property (logical) indicating whether ID token cryptographically verified OAuth flow. oauth_module_server(): Now surfaces error_uri provider error callbacks (RFC 6749, section 4.1.2.1). new $error_uri reactive field contains URI human-readable error page provider includes one; NULL otherwise. error_uri callback parameter also validated configurable size limit (e.g., options(shinyOAuth.callback_max_error_uri_bytes = 2048)). OAuth callback query cleanup now also applied early return paths internal function .process_query(), ensuring consistent cleanup. OAuth callback query size caps now enforced even user already authenticated. Previously, “token already present” branch .process_query() called .query_has_oauth_callback_keys() (parses query string) size validation, bypassing intended DoS guardrails. validate_untrusted_query_string() check now runs unconditionally top .process_query(). OAuth callback error responses (?error=...) now require valid state parameter. Missing/invalid/consumed state treated properly invalid_state error instead surfacing error ?error=... (set attacker). OAuth callback including iss query parameter now validate provider’s configured/discovered issuer callback processing (complementing existing ID token iss claim validation occurs post-exchange) (per RFC 9207). mismatch produces issuer_mismatch error audit event, defending authorization-server mix-attacks multi-provider scenarios. iss absent, current behavior retained (enforcement). handle_callback(): longer accepts decrypted_payload state_store_values bypass parameters. parameters intended internal use oauth_module_server()’s async path. can misused direct/custom callers bypass important security checks, moved internal-helper function (handle_callback_internal()). handle_callback()/refresh_token(): token response omits expires_in, warning now emitted per phase (exchange_code / refresh_token) operators know proactive token refresh trigger. Users can now also set finite default lifetime tokens via options(shinyOAuth.default_expires_in = <seconds>); unset, shinyOAuth now falls back 3600 seconds. get_userinfo() now supports JWT-encoded userinfo responses per OIDC Core, section 5.3.2. endpoint returns Content-Type: application/jwt, body decoded JWT. Verification fail-closed: signature verification always performed provider JWKS using provider’s allowed_algs, alg=none always rejected, unparseable headers, non-asymmetric algorithms, missing issuer/JWKS infrastructure raise errors. options(shinyOAuth.allow_unsigned_userinfo_jwt = TRUE) permits unsigned JWTs. New userinfo_signed_jwt_required property OAuthProvider (default FALSE) mandates userinfo endpoint returns application/jwt content-type subject verification. client_bearer_req() now validates target URL is_ok_host() attaching Bearer token. Relative URLs, plain HTTP non-loopback hosts, hosts outside options(shinyOAuth.allowed_hosts) rejected default. new check_url argument (default TRUE) allows opting check URL already validated. err_http() now extracts RFC 6749 section 5.2 structured error fields (error, error_description, error_uri) JSON error response bodies. fields surfaced error message bullets, attached condition object (oauth_error, oauth_error_description, oauth_error_uri), included trace/audit events. improves debugging token endpoint failures (e.g. invalid_grant, invalid_client) without changing existing control flow. OIDC claims parameter support (OIDC Core, section 5.5): OAuthClient oauth_client() now accept claims argument request specific claims userinfo Endpoint /ID token. Pass list structure (automatically JSON-encoded) pre-encoded JSON string. OIDC openid scope enforcement: provider issuer set (indicating OIDC) openid missing client’s scopes, build_auth_url() now auto-prepends emits one-time warning. OIDC discovery (oauth_provider_oidc_discover()) now prefers confidential auth methods (client_secret_basic, client_secret_post) none advertised token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported. Previously, mixed metadata (e.g. none + client_secret_basic) PKCE enabled silently select public-client posture ("body" without credentials). Scope validation now aligns RFC 6749, section 3.3 scope-token grammar (NQSCHAR = %x21 / %x23-5B / %x5D-7E). previous regex rejected valid ASCII characters !, #, $, =, @, ~, others. printable ASCII except space, double-quote, backslash now accepted. JWT helpers (build_client_assertion(), resolve_client_assertion_audience()) now defense--depth scalar guards malformed property values cause subscript errors runtime. Audit events: audit_token_refresh: replaced non-informative had_refresh_token field (always TRUE post-mutation) refresh_token_rotated (indicates whether provider returned new refresh token).

title: shinyOAuth 0.2.0
text: Token revocation: tokens can now revoked Shiny session ends. Enable via revoke_on_session_end = TRUE oauth_module_server(). provider must expose revocation_url (auto-discovered OIDC, set manually via oauth_provider()). New exported function revoke_token(). Token introspection login: validate tokens via provider’s introspection endpoint login. Configure via introspect introspect_elements properties OAuthClient. provider must expose introspection_url (auto-discovered OIDC, set manually via oauth_provider()). DoS protection: callback query parameters state payload/browser token sizes validated expensive operations (e.g., hashing audit logs). Maximum size may configured via options(); see section ‘Size caps’ vignette("usage", package = "shinyOAuth"). DoS protection: rate-limited JWKS refresh: forced JWKS cache refreshes (triggered unknown kid) now rate-limited prevent abuse. JWKS pinning: pinning now enforced signature verification: previously, jwks_pins jwks_pin_mode = "" verified least one key JWKS matched pin, signature verification still use matching key (pinned ). Now, signature verification restricted use keys whose thumbprints appear pin list, ensuring true key pinning rather presence-checks. use_shinyOAuth() now injects <meta name="referrer" content="-referrer"> default reduce leaking ?code=…&state=… via Referer header callback page. Can disabled use_shinyOAuth(inject_referrer_meta = FALSE). Sensitive outbound HTTP requests (token exchange/refresh, introspection, revocation, userinfo, OIDC discovery, JWKS) now default disable redirect following reject 3xx responses prevent bypassing host/HTTPS policies. Configurable via options(shinyOAuth.allow_redirect = TRUE). client_bearer_req() also gains follow_redirect, defaults FALSE, similarly control redirect behavior requests using bearer tokens. State now also consumed login failure paths (provider returns error also state). Callback URL parameters now also cleared login failure paths. OAuthProvider now requires absolute URLs (scheme + hostname) endpoint URLs. Provider fingerprint now includes userinfo_url introspection_url, reducing risk misconfiguration multiple providers share endpoints. state_payload_max_age property OAuthClient independent freshness validation state payload’s issued_at timestamp. Default client assertion JWT TTL reduced 5 minutes 120 seconds, reducing window replay attacks allowing clock skew.

title: shinyOAuth 0.2.0
text: New audit events: session_ended (logged Shiny session close), authenticated_changed (logged authentication status changes), token_introspection (introspect_token() used), token_revocation (revoke_token() used), error_state_consumed error_state_consumption_failed (called provider returns error callback handling state attempted consumed). audit events now include $process_id, $is_async, $main_process_id (called async worker); fields help identify process generated event whether async worker. Async workers now also properly propagate audit hooks main process (see ‘Fixed’). Audit event login_success now includes sub_source indicate whether subject digest came userinfo, id_token (verified), id_token_unverified. Audit digest keying: audit/event digests (e.g., sub_digest, browser_token_digest) now default HMAC-SHA256 auto-generated per-process key reduce reidentification/correlation risk logs leak. Configure key options(shinyOAuth.audit_digest_key = "..."), disable keying (legacy deterministic SHA-256) options(shinyOAuth.audit_digest_key = FALSE). HTTP log sanitization: sensitive data HTTP contexts (headers, cookies) now sanitized default audit logs. Can disabled options(shinyOAuth.audit_redact_http = FALSE). Use options(shinyOAuth.audit_include_http = FALSE) include HTTP data logs.

title: shinyOAuth 0.2.0
text: Configurable scope validation: validate_scopes property OAuthClient controls whether returned scopes validated requested scopes ("strict", "warn", "none"). Scopes now normalized (alphabetically sorted) comparison. OAuthProvider: extra parameters now blocked overriding reserved keys essential OAuth 2.0/OIDC flow. Reserved keys may explicitly overridden via options(shinyOAuth.unblock_auth_params = c(...), shinyOAuth.unblock_token_params = c(...), shinyOAuth.unblock_token_headers = c(...)). also validated early parameters named, catching configuration errors sooner. Added warning negative expires_in values token responses. Added warning OAuthClient instantiated inside Shiny session; may cause sealed state payload decryption fail random secret generated upon client creation. Added hints error messages sealed state payload decryption fails. Ensured clearer error message token response unexpected format. Ensured clearer error retrieved state store entry unexpected format. Ensured clearer error message retrieved userinfo parsed JSON. Immediate error OAuthProvider uses HS* algorithm options(shinyOAuth.allow_hs = TRUE) enabled; also immediate error OAuthProvider uses HS* algorithm ID token verification can happen client_secret absent weak. build_auth_url() now uses package-typed errors (err_invalid_state()) instead generic stopifnot() assertions, ensuring consistent error handling audit logging.

title: shinyOAuth 0.2.0
text: ID token signature/claims validation now occurs fetching userinfo. ensures cryptographic validation passes making external calls userinfo endpoint. fetching JWKS, key_ops present keys, keys key_ops including "verify" considered. oauth_provider() now defaults allowed_token_types c("Bearer") providers. prevents accidentally misusing non-Bearer tokens (e.g., DPoP, MAC) Bearer tokens. Set allowed_token_types = character() opt . Token type also now validated calling userinfo endpoint. client_assertion_audience property OAuthClient allows overriding JWT audience claim client assertion authentication.

title: shinyOAuth 0.2.0
text: Package now correctly requires httr2 >= 1.1.0. authenticated now flips FALSE promptly token expires reauth_after_seconds elapses, even without reactive changes. Previously, value remain TRUE past expiry unrelated reactive update triggered re-evaluation. HTTP error responses (4xx/5xx) now correctly returned caller immediately instead misclassified transport errors retried. Async worker options propagation: R options now automatically propagated async workers using async = TRUE. Previously, options set main process (including audit_hook, trace_hook, HTTP settings, custom options) available future::multisession workers. oauth_provider_microsoft(): fixed incorrect default blocked multi-tenant configuration. oauth_provider_oidc_discover(): stricter host matching; ? * wildcards now correctly handled. Fixed potential auto-redirect loop authentication error surfaced. Fixed potential race condition proactive refresh expiry watcher: expiry watcher now defers clearing token triggering reauthentication refresh progress. Token expiry handling token refresh now aligns handled login. State payload issued_at validation now applies clock drift leeway (OAuthProvider@leeway / shinyOAuth.leeway option), consistent ID token iat check.
